title: UK competition body probes hyperscaler security and cloud lock-in
byline: Giacomo Lee This article originally appeared
html:
The UK upped its digital sovereignty drive with a call for evidence into cloud developers' use of Kubernetes and identity and access management (IAM) services.

A questionnaire launched by the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) aims to probe vendor lock-in amongst the hyperscalers. The regulator's call referenced its work with Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Microsoft to lower egress fees and improve interoperability of their pair’s cloud platforms.

Microsoft is currently under the CMA microscope on whether it should be designated strategic market status (SMS) in respect of its business software ecosystem. A similar consultation on this matter ended last week.

AWS, meanwhile, was given mostly the all-clear in spring, having satisfied the CMA that it was improving vendor interoperability and reducing lock-in for British cloud users. AWS’ efforts on this front have seen it introduce AWS Interconnect, which can connect with Azure, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), and Google Cloud Platform (GCP).

With the new consultation including IAM in its scope, Amazon’s identity offerings will come under the spotlight alongside Microsoft’s IAM offering in Entra ID. Google and Oracle offer similar services with their cloud offerings.

Global IAM rivals outside the hyperscale stable include Okta and Palo Alto Networks with its Idira platform, as borne from the security vendor’s blockbuster CyberArk acquisition last year.

According to CMA data, Microsoft commanded 60–70 percent of the British security software market in 2025, with Amazon, Google, and Palo Alto Networks at zero to five percent. Okta, CrowdStrike, and Ping Identity trail Microsoft in second place at five-ten percent.

The CMA consultation, which is available to stakeholders both in and outside the U.K., closes on December 3 of this year.
summary: CMA continues digital sovereignty investigation with consultation into IAM and Kubernetes
